neighbours.label: rotation of an object: the verb or object at the point where something is rotated or turned around ('rotated', 'Rotate', 'turn it around')
fire: In the editor, select the image and rotate it ninety degrees to the right.
The figure shows a square rotated by forty-five degrees about its center.
To install the seat, lift it off the base, turn it around and click it back in.
The baby is rotated through ninety degrees as it passes down the birth canal.
He slowly rotated the key in the lock until he heard a click.
If the photo looks sideways, just rotate the phone and it will flip.
The dancer spun on one foot, turning a full circle before she landed.
The planet rotates on its axis once every twenty-four hours.
quiet: In the editor, select the image and move it a little to the right.
The figure shows a square shifted by two units along the x axis.
To install the seat, lift it off the base, clean it and click it back in.
The baby is carried in a sling for most of the long walk home.
He slowly pushed the key into the lock until he heard a click.
If the photo looks dark, just raise the brightness and it will improve.
The dancer leapt across the stage before she landed on one foot.
The planet travels around its star once every three hundred days.

notes: Card: ' rotated' x3, ' Rotate', 'turn it around', a wheel that 'leans' out, 'triangle rotated by 60 degrees'. Near misses move objects in the same scenes without rotating them.
